ModMetaData.description:
Discord Community: https://discord.gg/eVBebZ2N9s Version: v0.7.0 (Target: RimWorld 1.6)
RimSynapse - Regions and Territories Official Wiki and Documentation: https://github.com/RimSynapse/Regions-and-Territories/wiki
Handles mapping dynamics, including dynamic geographic province generation, world map overlays, regional faction territory control, population density mapping, road generation, and ruins placement.
*** BEST ON A NEW COLONY - EXISTING SAVES ARE SUPPORTED IN COMPATIBILITY MODE ***
Regions and Territories does most of its work during world generation. It draws the province boundaries and then places faction settlements according to them, respecting region occupancy limits, border buffers, and sequential expansion. A world generated with the mod installed gets all of that.
Added to a world that already exists, it adopts that world in Compatibility Mode instead. Provinces are still drawn, territory is still owned and shown on the map modes, and everything the overlays display works as normal. What stands down is placement: the mod will not decide where settlements and outposts may be built, because your world is already full of towns that were placed with no regard for those rules, and enforcing them now would refuse ground that has been settled since long before the mod arrived. Vanilla and any other mods keep control of placement, and more than one settlement may share a province.
The mode is decided once, per save, and recorded in it. You can see and change it under Strict territorial ownership in the mod settings while that save is loaded - but be aware that switching an in-progress world to strict starts applying rules to settlements that were never placed under them.
A new colony is still the recommended way to play this mod. Compatibility mode exists so an existing save is usable, not so it is equivalent - geography-driven faction placement, region occupancy limits, border buffers and sequential expansion are the heart of what Regions and Territories does, and only a world generated with the mod installed gets them.
Removing the mod from an in-progress save will log errors about missing province data the next time that save is loaded. The save will usually still open, but this is not a supported path and you should expect a wall of red text.
Requires: Map Mode Framework
--- Roadmap --- 0.8 - Demographics, News and Narrative Voice: Regional ideological demographics - a per-region belief-distribution model, pawns generated from it, a migrating dwelling heatmap, Empire hiring cost and resource overlays tied to regional population, plus world-gen options (land coverage and multiple continents) and livable ruins. 0.9 - Factions and Living Societies: Deeper placement and territory governance feeding the Factions layer. 0.10 - Cross-Mod Capability Passes: Another pass over how territory drives the whole set. These ship when they are ready - no dates.
--- Changelog (v0.7.0) - Regions and Territories Compatibility --- - NEW - Mod-agnostic world object integration: Empire Refactored, Vanilla Outposts Expanded, Vanilla Expanded Framework and World Domination are recognised through adapter profiles instead of by name, so territory rules no longer hardcode which mods exist. - NEW - Placement and territory governance: one evaluator decides where settlements, outposts, military installations and camps may stand, and the world inspect pane tells you why a tile was refused. - NEW - Compatibility mode: a world generated before this mod is adopted rather than refused, and you are told when that happens. - Fixed: Empire settlement population always read as zero. Three of the four adapter profiles named members or types that do not exist on the real assemblies, and nothing said so - a wrong name cost no error, it just returned a plausible zero. - Fixed: Vanilla Expanded Framework renamed its assembly from VFECore to VEF, so that profile had resolved to nothing for as long as it had existed. - Changed: the demographic component of territory ownership contributes nothing this release. It was awarding a fifth of the score for simply owning a settlement, which the settlement score already counted. It returns in 0.8 reading real regional demographics. - REQUIRES A NEW COLONY - not save-game compatible.
Full version history: https://github.com/RimSynapse/Regions-and-Territories/wiki/Changelog
